# Project Overview: Machine Minds Manipulator - Ragdoll Simulator

## Files Needed

### 1. `MachineMindsManiputlator.java`
**Purpose**: Main game class containing all game logic, rendering, physics integration, and input handling

**Key Components**:
- **Main class**: `MachineMindsManiputlator` (extends JFrame or JPanel for rendering)
- **Physics engine integration**: Wrapper for external physics library (dyn4j recommended)
- **Rendering system**: Custom paint method for drawing ragdoll and background
- **Input handler**: MouseListener and MouseMotionListener implementation
- **Ragdoll model**: Data structure representing Rick Astley character with joints and rigid bodies

**Key Functions**:
- `main()` - Entry point, initializes game window
- `init()` - Sets up physics world, creates ragdoll, loads/creates Rick Astley image
- `update(deltaTime)` - Physics simulation step
- `render(Graphics g)` - Draws everything to screen
- `mousePressed(MouseEvent e)` - Handles click down for grabbing
- `mouseDragged(MouseEvent e)` - Applies forces to dragged body part
- `mouseReleased(MouseEvent e)` - Releases grabbed body part
- `createRagdoll()` - Constructs ragdoll with bodies, joints, and constraints
- `drawRagdoll(Graphics g)` - Renders ragdoll bodies and Rick Astley image overlay
- `drawTShirtText(Graphics g)` - Renders t-shirt text on character

**Key Variables**:
- `World physicsWorld` - Physics simulation world
- `List<Body> ragdollBodies` - All rigid bodies making up ragdoll
- `List<Joint> ragdollJoints` - Joints connecting bodies
- `Body grabbedBody` - Currently grabbed body part (null if none)
- `MouseJoint mouseJoint` - Temporary joint for mouse interaction
- `BufferedImage rickAstleyImage` - Character sprite/texture
- `int windowWidth, windowHeight` - Display dimensions

## Physics Library Recommendation

**dyn4j** - 2D Java physics engine (https://dyn4j.org/)
- Rigid body dynamics
- Joints and constraints
- Collision detection
- Easy integration

## How to Proceed

1. **I will present this skeleton** - You review and approve by saying "continue", "y", or "go on"
2. **I will provide pseudocode overview** - Detailed logic flow for all functions
3. **You approve pseudocode** - Same approval keywords
4. **I deliver code section by section**:
   - Imports and class declaration
   - Main method and initialization
   - Ragdoll creation logic
   - Physics update loop
   - Rendering methods
   - Input handling
   - Helper methods
5. **You approve each section** - I move to next section
6. **If you say "no", "n", "context", "goco", or "try again"** - I revise current section

## Notes

- Single file implementation
- Requires dyn4j library in classpath
- Rick Astley image will be procedurally generated or simple placeholder
- T-shirt text rendered as overlay
- 60 FPS target with game loop

**Ready for your approval to proceed to pseudocode phase.**
